newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Brazil sees more Venezuelan oil imports - diplomat. [CORRECTED 22:24 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees more Venezuelan oil imports - diplomat. [CORRECTED 22:24 GMT]

text.p: Brazil is hoping to increase its imports of Venezuelan crude oil and refined products by 15,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of the year, a diplomatic spokesman said on Monday.

"We are hoping to increase our imports to $900 million this year," said a spokesman for Brazil's Trade Minister Francisco Dornelles after a conference in Caracas (corrects to make clear Dornelles is Brazil's Trade Minister, not the spokesman).
Venezuela and Brazil are also considering buying or leasing a refinery in Latin America as a means of increasing trade between the two countries.
"There's been no decision about where it would be yet, but it could be in the Caribbean," Dornelles said.
He said the president of state-run Petroleos de Venezuela, Luis Giusti, would visit Brazil's Petrobras this month to further the talks.

PDVSA and Petrobras had planned to build a refinery in northern Brazil, but the idea was shelved after the costs were worked out. The diplomat said they were now considering constructing an oil products import terminal in northern Brazil.
